title: Self-contained gate-elimination pair (2, 1) for MOD3

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"MOD3 family defined in proof.md: for every integer n>=0 and x in {0,1}^n, f_n(x)=1 iff x_1+...+x_n is congruent to 0 modulo 3 (so f_0=1). The language L={x : the number of ones in x is divisible by 3} is decided by one fixed linear-time algorithm, with NP verifier V(x,w)=1 iff w is empty and the Hamming weight of x is divisible by 3, and witness bound W(n)=0.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"2"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"2"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one total uniform polynomial-time family (hence in NP with empty witnesses), C_B2(f_n)>=2n-4 for every integer n>=2 in the full Li-Yang B2 model (all 16 binary gates, unrestricted fan-out and depth, constant nodes free, every gate counted), at actual input length n=|x|; consequently liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=2.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: Lemma (proved in proof.md, Theorem 6.1): for every integer m>=2 and every residue s modulo 3, every B2 circuit computing M_{m,s}(x)=[x_1+...+x_m = s mod 3] has at least 2m-4 gates.
